title: Librarian: a Wikipedia page, made readable

scenes.say: This is a real Wikipedia page. Every sentence is correct, and almost no one can read it.
Give Librarian the link, and it redraws the whole page as shapes: why the idea exists, what it is, the parts it's made of. Each piece points back to the paragraph it came from.
The rest of the page follows, section by section, as diagrams instead of walls of notation.
But most of us meet ideas like this in a lecture. Stop it where it loses you, and box the part you don't follow.
Then call the librarian. Point at anything, and ask. (Then the call itself: three questions, three answers.)

And it doesn't make things up. The notebook it found is one someone actually wrote and ran. Around it: lecture notes from university courses, talks by the people who work on this, and the papers themselves. Each is credited and linked.
One page, one lecture, one conversation, grown into one explanation.
Librarian. Grow one explanation, from every source.
